name: Biyo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Jing, Dian 2015. Mojiang biyue Haniyu cankao yufa [Biyo Hani reference grammar, full grammar per Glottolog] — Chinese-published, not found online

sources.citation: Namkung, Ju (ed.). 1996. Phonological inventories of Tibeto-Burman languages. STEDT Monograph 3. Berkeley: STEDT.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Hani: Biyue (Caiyuan, Mojiang) pp. 130-131, data from Sun et al. 1991 ZMYYC #30 (pp. 271-273) and Li & Wang 1986 (pp. 129-142): tones ma55 high level, ma33 mid level, ma31 low falling, ma35 high rising (mainly Chinese loans); Hani: Biyue p. 132 from Hansson 1989. No stress/accent remark in the entire Hani section (secondary compilation).

sources.citation: Hansson, Inga-Lill. 1989. A comparison of Akha, Hani, Khatu and Pijɔ. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 12(1): 6-91.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pijɔ (= Biyue, one Mojiang informant, p. 7) phoneme tables p. 8: three non-laryngealized tones High/Mid/Low plus laryngealized Mid/Low; 'The tonal systems of Khatu and Pijɔ correspond exactly to Akha and Hani. The low tone is in all of them slightly falling. Some differences in the tones may depend on sandhi rules, which remain to be worked out.' No word 'stress' or 'accent' anywhere in the scanned pp. 6-25 (rest of article is correspondence sets).

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) languages: a study from the perspectives of shared innovation and phylogenetic estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington.

sources.note: Open-access comparative dissertation with Biyo data and per-language phonological notes; would confirm silence or supply a remark on stress.

sources.citation: Wheatley, Julian K. 1982. Comments on the 'Hani' dialects of Loloish. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 7(1): 1-37.

sources.note: Discusses Biyue initials, tense/lax vowels and finals from Hu & Dai's data; silent on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent|accent = 0 hits).
